title: The Contact Lens Crisis

patient.name: Ms Priya Nair
patient.presenting_complaint: Right eye red, painful and watery since this morning — fell asleep in contact lenses last night

history.hpc: Ms Priya presents to the eye casualty with a 12-hour history of right eye redness, pain, and watering. She admits to falling asleep in her monthly disposable contact lenses last night after a late study session. She woke up with her eye stuck shut and extremely painful. There is no discharge but the eye is very watery. She has significant photophobia and reports that her vision is blurry. She denies any trauma or foreign body sensation prior to sleeping.
history.social_hx: University student, wears monthly disposable contact lenses daily for 2 years, admits to occasionally sleeping in lenses, non-smoker

iop.right: Not measured — corneal ulcer present, defer tonometry

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right: conjunctival injection ++, circumcorneal ciliary flush, 4mm x 3mm central corneal ulcer with dense white infiltrate and surrounding stromal oedema, epithelial defect confirmed on fluorescein staining (stains green under cobalt blue light), moderate anterior chamber reaction — 1+ cells. Left: clear.

fundus.right: Deferred — patient in significant pain, corneal pathology is the focus

investigations.corneal_scrape: Performed under slit lamp: material sent for Gram stain, bacterial culture and sensitivity, fungal culture
investigations.gram_stain: Gram-negative rods — consistent with Pseudomonas aeruginosa (pending culture confirmation)
investigations.fluorescein_staining: Positive — confirms epithelial defect overlying infiltrate
investigations.contact_lens_culture: Patient's lens case submitted — Pseudomonas aeruginosa grown (pending)

diagnosis: Bacterial keratitis (Pseudomonas aeruginosa) right eye secondary to contact lens wear, specifically sleeping in contact lenses.

immediate: Remove contact lens immediately if still in place
Corneal scrape for culture and sensitivity before starting antibiotics
Intensive topical fluoroquinolone: ciprofloxacin 0.3% or moxifloxacin 0.5% — every 30 minutes day and night for first 48 hours (waking patient overnight)
Oral analgesia: paracetamol 1g QDS for pain
Admit or arrange next-day review — central corneal ulcer near visual axis requires close monitoring
Cyclopentolate 1% BD — for ciliary spasm pain relief
follow_up: Review at 24–48 hours: assess ulcer size, infiltrate density, and anterior chamber reaction
Adjust antibiotic frequency based on clinical response (reduce as improvement seen)
Corneal scrape results guide antibiotic choice if not responding to empirical therapy
Avoid topical steroids until infection is controlled (risk of worsening)
No contact lens wear until fully healed — reassess suitability for future lens wear
patient_education: Sleeping in contact lenses is a major risk factor for bacterial keratitis — never sleep in lenses
Replace lenses on the schedule recommended — monthly lenses must be replaced monthly
Proper hygiene: wash hands before handling lenses, clean lens case daily with fresh solution
If eyes become red, painful, or blurry while wearing lenses — remove immediately and seek review
This infection can cause permanent corneal scarring — early treatment is critical

key_points: Asks about contact lens wear and sleeping in lenses — key risk factor
Elicits onset, duration, and nature of pain (photophobia, foreign body sensation)
Asks about discharge vs watering — bacterial ulcer typically has watering/mucopurulent discharge
Asks about prior lens hygiene habits and lens type
Slit lamp examination with fluorescein staining to confirm epithelial defect
Corneal scrape for Gram stain and culture before starting antibiotics
Defers IOP measurement over active ulcer
Correctly identifies bacterial keratitis (not viral or Acanthamoeba)
Links to contact lens sleeping — identifies mechanism
Recognises Pseudomonas from Gram-negative rods result
Intensive topical fluoroquinolone — correct frequency (every 30 min initially)
Close follow-up given central location near visual axis
